hints: Calculate the gradient of line segment $AB$: $m_{AB} = \dfrac{5 - 1}{4 - 1}$.
Calculate the gradient of line segment $BC$: $m_{BC} = \dfrac{8 - 5}{0 - 4}$.
Multiply the two gradients: show that $m_{AB} \times m_{BC} = \dfrac{4}{3} \times \left(-\dfrac{3}{4}\right) = -1$.
walkthrough:
A gradient product of minus one proves a right angle.
Calculate the gradients of segments $AB$ and $BC$:
$$m_{AB} = \dfrac{5 - 1}{4 - 1} = \dfrac{4}{3}$$
$$m_{BC} = \dfrac{8 - 5}{0 - 4} = \dfrac{3}{-4} = -\dfrac{3}{4}$$

Multiply the two gradients to test for perpendicularity:
$$m_{AB} \times m_{BC} = \dfrac{4}{3} \times \left(-\dfrac{3}{4}\right) = -1$$
Since their gradient product is $-1$, $AB \perp BC$, so triangle $ABC$ is right-angled at $B$.
